long_biography.plain_text:
Spiliadis left Patras as a young student, continued sociology studies in Montreal and helped establish Radio Centre-Ville for immigrant communities. Frustrated that local restaurants reduced Greece’s culinary tradition to familiar stereotypes, he used a bank loan to open his first dining room in 1979. The idea centred on pristine ingredients, simple preparation, shared plates and a visible fish market.

Rather than franchise or depend on outside capital, Spiliadis financed measured growth from operating cash flow and retained ownership with his family. That discipline carried Milos into major cities across Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. His hospitality platform later extended to an Athens boutique hotel and other Greek experiences. Spiliadis continues to shape Milos through its ingredient networks, restaurant craft and deliberate presentation of Greek culture.
